GEOG 103.description: A survey of the principles and methods of geographic inquiry. Not required for the geography major.
GEOG 103.subject: GEOG
GEOG 103.title: Foundations of Geography

GEOG 104.description: Basic concepts of landform geography, climatology and meteorology, and biogeography.
GEOG 104.subject: GEOG
GEOG 104.title: Introduction to Physical Geography

GEOG 105.description: Introduction to geographic data; use of digital maps and aerial/satellite images as means of Earth observation; basics of spatial data analysis; location-based Web APPs; digital map services.
GEOG 105.subject: GEOG
GEOG 105.title: The Digital Earth

GEOG 121.description: Introduction to processes of political, economic, social, and environmental change around the world; topics include geopolitical transitions, nationalism, trade, uneven development, conflict, environmental geopolitics, and demographic change, with an emphasis on non-U.S. contexts.
GEOG 121.subject: GEOG
GEOG 121.title: Geographies of Global Change

GEOG 201.description: Hydrology, soil science, and interpretation of physical features formed by water, wind, and ice, with emphasis on environmental change. Three hours of lecture and one two-hour laboratory per week.
GEOG 201.subject: GEOG
GEOG 201.title: Landform Geography

GEOG 202.description: Processes that influence weather and climate patterns on the earth. Three lectures and one two-hour laboratory per week.
GEOG 202.subject: GEOG
GEOG 202.title: Weather and Climate

GEOG 221.description: An intensive regional analysis of South Carolina. Selected phenomena such as urbanization, industrialization, land use, the physical environment, and their interrelationships.
GEOG 221.subject: GEOG
GEOG 221.title: Geography of South Carolina

GEOG 223.description: Physical and human geography of Latin America.
GEOG 223.subject: GEOG
GEOG 223.title: Geography of Latin America

GEOG 224.description: Physical and human geography of North America with emphasis on the United States.
GEOG 224.subject: GEOG
GEOG 224.title: Geography of North America

GEOG 225.description: Physical and human geography of Europe.
GEOG 225.subject: GEOG
GEOG 225.title: Geography of Europe

GEOG 226.description: A regional geographic approach to the environmental, social, economic, and political aspects of the Middle East (Southwest Asia and north Africa) with emphasis on contemporary problems.
GEOG 226.subject: GEOG
GEOG 226.title: Geography of the Middle East

GEOG 227.description: A geographical investigation of the historical, cultural, political, and economic processes that shape Central Asian states and societies from antiquity, through periods of colonialism and empire, the formation of the Soviet Union, and into the current context of globalization and international development.
GEOG 227.subject: GEOG
GEOG 227.title: Geography of Russia and Central Asia

GEOG 228.description: A regional approach to the physical, social, economic, and political aspects of Sub-Saharan Africa with emphasis on contemporary problems.
GEOG 228.subject: GEOG
GEOG 228.title: Geography of Sub-Saharan Africa

GEOG 263.description: Introduction to principles and methods of geographic information systems including discussion of computers, spatial data, analysis, and display. Includes discussion of applications and hands-on experience.
GEOG 263.subject: GEOG
GEOG 263.title: Geographic Information Systems

GEOG 285.description: This course is an introduction to the use of small unmanned aerial systems (UAS) in collecting/processing imagery for mapping/information analysis. Course content includes UAS characteristics, small camera considerations, project planning and processing, and legal requirements in the United States and selected European countries.
GEOG 285.subject: GEOG
GEOG 285.title: Introduction to Drones for Airborne Spatial Data

GEOG 305.description: Global patterns and processes of migration through multi-disciplinary perspectives, addressing the types, causes, and effects of migration. Possible topics include labor migration, refugees and asylum, climate migration, migration controls, and processes of inclusion and exclusion.
GEOG 305.subject: GEOG
GEOG 305.title: Global Migration

GEOG 310.description: Selected topics of special interest in geography. May be repeated as content varies by title.
GEOG 310.subject: GEOG
GEOG 310.title: Topics in Geography

GEOG 311.description: The temporal-spatial relationship between humans and the natural environment with emphasis on the role through time of human activity in changing the face of the earth.
GEOG 311.subject: GEOG
GEOG 311.title: Landscape and Cultural Geography

GEOG 312.description: Geographic perspectives on problems in international relations. Political geographic analysis of contemporary world problems.
GEOG 312.subject: GEOG
GEOG 312.title: Geography and Global Geopolitics

GEOG 313.description: Spatial interrelation and linking of economic activities and how location affects the nature of economic systems.
GEOG 313.subject: GEOG
GEOG 313.title: Economic Geography

GEOG 314.description: An overview of conflict, displacement, and humanitarianism in the context of the modern interstate-system. Topics include refoulment, border externalization, transit, resettlement, and asylum politics.
GEOG 314.subject: GEOG
GEOG 314.title: Geopolitics and Refugees

GEOG 319.description: An overview of historical and contemporary urban development and growth, with an emphasis on post-colonial and non-Western contexts.
GEOG 319.subject: GEOG
GEOG 319.title: Cities in a Changing World

GEOG 320.description: Investigation of human-environment interactions and their effects on global population health and health disparities through the lens of Health and Medical geography.
GEOG 320.subject: GEOG
GEOG 320.title: Global Health Geographies

GEOG 321.description: Overview of the relationships between urbanization and environmental processes and an exploration of pathways to greater sustainability.
GEOG 321.subject: GEOG
GEOG 321.title: Sustainable Cities

GEOG 324.description: Geographic change through time in the United States, with emphasis on evolution of the American landscape. Physical environment as modified by human intervention over time within a regional framework.
GEOG 324.subject: GEOG
GEOG 324.title: Landscapes of the United States

GEOG 330.description: The study of disasters, their triggering mechanisms (natural, human, technological), their spatial distributions from local to global scales, and associated human responses.
GEOG 330.subject: GEOG
GEOG 330.title: Disasters

GEOG 341.description: Introduction to the theory and principles of map construction including discussions of equipment and materials, lettering and symbolization, scale and generalization, data manipulation and representation. Presentation of geographic information on maps.
GEOG 341.subject: GEOG
GEOG 341.title: Cartography

GEOG 343.description: A geographic consideration of the interactions between environment and society. The ways in which social, economic, and cultural processes interact across local to global scales and influence environmental practices, policies, and patterns of change will be emphasized.
GEOG 343.subject: GEOG
GEOG 343.title: Environment and Society

GEOG 344.description: Overview of the development of American cities from industrial period to the present. Special attention given to the political, economic, social processes that shape urban space and urban ways of life.
GEOG 344.subject: GEOG
GEOG 344.title: Geographies of American Cities

GEOG 345.description: Basics of remote sensing and image interpretation in aerial photography, drone technology and satellite imagery for earth observations. Emphasis on competent use of remote sensing data for a variety of geographic and multidisciplinary applications.
GEOG 345.subject: GEOG
GEOG 345.title: Introduction to Remote Sensing

GEOG 346.description: Major theories and methodologies for studying the relationship between climate and society.
GEOG 346.subject: GEOG
GEOG 346.title: Climate and Society

GEOG 347.description: Introduction to spatial and institutional aspects of water availability, demand, and quality. Water storage/conveyance strategies and facilities. Real and perceived flood, drought hazards.
GEOG 347.subject: GEOG
GEOG 347.title: Water as a Resource

GEOG 348.description: Spatial distributions of plants and animals as they relate to historical biogeographic patterns and human impact on the biosphere.
GEOG 348.subject: GEOG
GEOG 348.title: Biogeography

GEOG 349.description: Introduction to theories and principles of cartographic animation.
GEOG 349.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOG 341 or GEOG 263.
GEOG 349.subject: GEOG
GEOG 349.title: Cartographic Animation

GEOG 360.description: Fundamental principles of wind formation, measurement, and its impacts on the natural and human environment – landscape, human settlement and health, transportation, and energy.
GEOG 360.subject: GEOG
GEOG 360.title: Geography of Wind

GEOG 365.description: Atmospheric circulation, structure, and processes of tropical climates and hurricanes. Forecasting and model simulations of hurricanes. Temporal variations of tropical climate change and hurricanes.
GEOG 365.subject: GEOG
GEOG 365.title: Hurricanes and Tropical Climatology

GEOG 370.description: Resource, managerial, and recreational-use components of the national park system; contemporary issues, problems, and managerial alternatives.
GEOG 370.subject: GEOG
GEOG 370.title: America’s National Parks

GEOG 371.description: Fundamentals, processes, and issues that relate to air pollution. Emphasis is on the role of the atmosphere. Additional topics include pollution sources, environmental and health effects of air pollution, air quality measurements, urban smog, and ozone depletion, regulations, and societal impacts.
GEOG 371.subject: GEOG
GEOG 371.title: Air Pollution Fundamentals

GEOG 380.description: Geopolitical, historical, cultural, and economic geographies of human rights around the world; issues of development, environment, health, inequality, violence.
GEOG 380.subject: GEOG
GEOG 380.title: Global Human Rights

GEOG 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
GEOG 399.subject: GEOG
GEOG 399.title: Independent Study

GEOG 495.description: Research methods and projects; restricted to students with at least 15 hours of credit in geography. Restricted to students with at least 15 hours of credit in geography.
GEOG 495.subject: GEOG
GEOG 495.title: Seminar in Geography

GEOG 497.description: Service learning experience in conjunction with designated Geography courses. Direct, hands-on service experience with an agency, voluntary organization, or community-based project. May be repeated, as content varies by title. Students enrolled in designated Geography courses by Instructor permission.
GEOG 497.subject: GEOG
GEOG 497.title: Special Topics: Service Learning in Geography

GEOG 498.description: Research on a significant geography problem in the local environment. Emphasis will be on the development of relatively individualized experiences in scientific investigation.
GEOG 498.subject: GEOG
GEOG 498.title: Undergraduate Research

GEOG 499.description: Senior research thesis on a problem of fundamental geographic significance, supervised by faculty member; must include a written final project report.
GEOG 499.subject: GEOG
GEOG 499.title: Senior Thesis

GEOG 510.description: Selected topics of special interest in geography. May be repeated as content varies by title.
GEOG 510.subject: GEOG
GEOG 510.title: Special Topics in Geographic Research

GEOG 511.description: Scientific approaches to locational problems in urban and regional planning, including regional growth and decline, land use control, public facility location and provision, and locational efficiency.
GEOG 511.subject: GEOG
GEOG 511.title: Planning and Locational Analysis

GEOG 512.description: A survey of the political, economic, and social causes and consequences of migration. Topics include immigration policy, border control, settlement patterns, transnationalism, multiculturalism, and integration. Selected contemporary and historical cases.
GEOG 512.subject: GEOG
GEOG 512.title: Migration and Globalization

GEOG 515.description: Concepts of space and power and their relationship to polities, elections, geopolitics, identities, law, economics, populations, and civil society.
GEOG 515.subject: GEOG
GEOG 515.title: Political Geography

GEOG 516.description: Analysis of the competing demands for limited resources in the coastal zone with emphasis on the role of management in the resolution of conflicts over resource use.
GEOG 516.subject: GEOG
GEOG 516.title: Coastal Zone Management

GEOG 517.description: A discussion-based seminar course that examines nature-society relations in coastal regions globally. The course will use social theory to understand how uneven development processes shaped – and continue shaping – current coastlines. We will explore key topics including coastal capitalism, delta ecologies, and climate justice via several global case studies.
GEOG 517.subject: GEOG
GEOG 517.title: Socionatural Coastlines in Global Perspective

GEOG 521.description: An examination of the factors responsible for creating the contemporary South Carolina cultural landscape.
GEOG 521.subject: GEOG
GEOG 521.title: Landscapes of South Carolina

GEOG 525.description: Analysis of transportation systems and the application of geographic tools to transportation planning.
GEOG 525.subject: GEOG
GEOG 525.title: Geographical Analysis of Transportation

GEOG 530.description: Human and environmental contributions to the generation and management of hazards originating from extreme natural events to technological failures. Contemporary public policy issues at the national and international level.
GEOG 530.subject: GEOG
GEOG 530.title: Environmental Hazards

GEOG 531.description: A survey of basic quantitative approaches for handling and interpreting geographically related data; univariate and bivariate procedures applicable to a variety of problems.
GEOG 531.subject: GEOG
GEOG 531.title: Quantitative Methods in Geographic Research

GEOG 535.description: Examination of the geo-spatial aspects of hazards analysis and planning with specific reference to disaster preparedness, recover, mitigation, and resilience.
GEOG 535.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: GEOG 363 and GEOG 530, or equivalents.
GEOG 535.subject: GEOG
GEOG 535.title: Hazards Analysis and Planning

GEOG 538.description: Political, social, and cultural landscapes of food and farming around the world; issues of agricultural production, trade, consumption, and food security.
GEOG 538.subject: GEOG
GEOG 538.title: Global Food Politics

GEOG 541.description: Planning, compiling, constructing, and evaluating thematic maps. Theory and practice in scribing, separation and screening, color proofing, and map reproduction. Discussions of the process of map communication and the ways the cartographer can improve that communication.
GEOG 541.subject: GEOG
GEOG 541.title: Advanced Cartography

GEOG 542.description: Theories and principles of interactive and animated cartographic design.
GEOG 542.subject: GEOG
GEOG 542.title: Dynamic Cartography

GEOG 544.description: The influence of political boundaries, historical forces, settlement patterns, and transportation processes on urban life.
GEOG 544.subject: GEOG
GEOG 544.title: Geography of the City

GEOG 545.description: Principles and controls of weather and climate as they occur at the regional/synoptic scale. Background on the critical tools and concepts used for daily weather forecasting by the National Weather Service and prominent government agencies, and used by broadcast meteorologists.
GEOG 545.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOG 202.
GEOG 545.subject: GEOG
GEOG 545.title: Weather Analysis and Forecasting

GEOG 546.description: Analysis of climate applications in natural and human-modified environments. Content may include water resources, solar energy, urban planning, air quality, agriculture, and tourism. Course work includes lab and field experimentation.
GEOG 546.subject: GEOG
GEOG 546.title: Applied Climatology

GEOG 547.description: Introduction to landforms and processes associated with flowing water at the earth’s surface. Hydrology, sedimentology, and theories of channel formation and drainage basin evolution.
GEOG 547.subject: GEOG
GEOG 547.title: Fluvial Geomorphology

GEOG 548.description: Analysis of emergent patterns in landscape structure and its linkage to ecological processes; application of relevant principles, methodologies, and geospatial technologies to solving real-world challenges focused on species and ecosystem conservation.
GEOG 548.subject: GEOG
GEOG 548.title: Landscape Ecology

GEOG 549.description: Spatial variation of hydrology, water quality, and water-related hazards, including runoff generation, soil erosion, sedimentation, and flood hazards. Emphasizes a watershed perspective using geographic data and methods.
GEOG 549.subject: GEOG
GEOG 549.title: Water and Watersheds

GEOG 551.description: Computer-assisted digital image analysis; Image correction; Spatial/spectral transformation; image classification and change detection; Use of remote sensing for solving real-world environmental problems.
GEOG 551.subject: GEOG
GEOG 551.title: Remote Sensing of the Environment

GEOG 552.description: Introduction to fundamental concepts used to map topographic and planimetric Earth surface features using digital LiDAR (LiDARgrammetric) and digital soft-copy photogrammetry (Photogrammetric).
GEOG 552.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOG 263, GEOG 341, GEOG 345, GEOG 551, GEOG 563, or graduate student standing.
GEOG 552.subject: GEOG
GEOG 552.title: LiDARgrammetric and Photogrammetric Digital Surface Mapping

GEOG 554.description: Computer programming of spatial problems; spatial statistical analysis, interactive graphics, and computer maps.
GEOG 554.subject: GEOG
GEOG 554.title: Spatial Programming

GEOG 556.description: Web-based Geographic Information Systems (WebGIS), including concepts and principles of WebGIS, web programming fundamentals, web-based mapping techniques, and developing WebGIS applications.
GEOG 556.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOG 263 or graduate student standing.
GEOG 556.subject: GEOG
GEOG 556.title: WebGIS

GEOG 561.description: Key concepts of geography and current approaches to teaching geography with specific attention to classroom materials, curriculum reform, cross-curricular integration, learning theory, and the use of geospatial/instructional technology.
GEOG 561.subject: GEOG
GEOG 561.title: Contemporary Issues in Geography Education

GEOG 562.description: Technology and use of Global Positioning Systems (GPS). GPS space segment, receiver technologies, range observables, and positioning accuracy. Applications to large/medium scale mapping, remote sensing, and aerial photography.
GEOG 562.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOG 345, GEOG 263, or GEOG 551 or graduate student standing.
GEOG 562.subject: GEOG
GEOG 562.title: Satellite Mapping and the Global Positioning System

GEOG 563.description: Theory and application of geographic information systems including discussions of automated input, storage, analysis, integration, and display of spatial data. Use of an operational geographic information system.
GEOG 563.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOG 263 or graduate student standing.
GEOG 563.subject: GEOG
GEOG 563.title: Advanced Geographic Information Systems

GEOG 564.description: Geographical information systems for modeling physical/human processes in space and time using raster and vector data. Cartographic modeling concepts, embedded models, and GIS-model coupling.
GEOG 564.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOG 263 or graduate student standing.
GEOG 564.subject: GEOG
GEOG 564.title: GIS-Based Modeling

GEOG 565.description: Representation, construction, maintenance, and analysis of spatial data in a geographic information system (GIS) database.
GEOG 565.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOG 263 or GEOG 341 or GEOG 551 or GEOG 563 or graduate student standing.
GEOG 565.subject: GEOG
GEOG 565.title: Geographic Information System (GIS) Databases and Their Use

GEOG 566.description: The processes of climate adaptation planning and management from central concepts in adaptation to issues such as projecting impacts, vulnerability assessment, coping with uncertainty, and decision making.
GEOG 566.subject: GEOG
GEOG 566.title: Climate Adaptation and Community Resilience Planning

GEOG 567.description: Climatic changes of the past and their impact on the physical landscape, with an emphasis on the Quaternary period.
GEOG 567.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in a 200-level course in physical geography or geology or equivalent.
GEOG 567.subject: GEOG
GEOG 567.title: Long-Term Environmental Change

GEOG 568.description: Consequences of increasing anthropogenic changes on environmental systems including the sources of change, regional impacts, and social and policy responses.
GEOG 568.subject: GEOG
GEOG 568.title: Human Dimensions of Global Environmental Change

GEOG 569.description: Intersections of international development and environmental change; study of general theoretical perspectives balanced with case studies from the Global South.
GEOG 569.subject: GEOG
GEOG 569.title: International Development and the Environment

GEOG 570.description: Geography of public land, water, and related public trust resources (wildlife, timber, minerals, fuels, recreation, wetlands, coastal zones, wilderness); historical geography of policy; spatial aspects of current research and management.
GEOG 570.subject: GEOG
GEOG 570.title: Geography of Public Land and Water Policy

GEOG 571.description: Field techniques and processes in the atmospheric boundary layer including radiation, soil heat fluxes, turbulence, momentum, latent and sensible heat fluxes, moisture, and evaporation.
GEOG 571.subject: GEOG
GEOG 571.title: Microclimatology

GEOG 573.description: Observations and theories of climatic change and variability as they occur at different space and time scales. Projections of future climates. Techniques used in climatic change research and impact analysis.
GEOG 573.subject: GEOG
GEOG 573.title: Climatic Change and Variability

GEOG 581.description: This course examines cultural understandings of and responses to globalization, examining topics such as its history and theories, migration, economic integration and inequality, identity, social movements, and the environment.
GEOG 581.subject: GEOG
GEOG 581.title: Globalization and Cultural Questions

GEOG 590.description: Influence of wind on coastal systems, with emphasis on nearshore currents, sediment transport and bedforms, aeolian transport, and dunes. Minimum Junior standing required.
GEOG 590.subject: GEOG
GEOG 590.title: Beach-Dune Interactions

GEOG 595.description: Internship in government agencies, private-sector businesses, and non-profit organizations under the joint supervision of sponsor and departmental. A maximum of three credits may be applied to undergraduate Geography major or to Geography master's degree. May be repeated to a maximum of six credits.
GEOG 595.subject: GEOG
GEOG 595.title: Internship in Geography

GEOG 701.description: A survey of the development of geographic philosophy and an analysis of geographic methodology.
GEOG 701.subject: GEOG
GEOG 701.title: History of Geographic Thought

GEOG 705.description: Directed research topics individually assigned and supervised by graduate faculty. May be repeated for credit.
GEOG 705.subject: GEOG
GEOG 705.title: Directed Individual Studies in Geography

GEOG 706.description: Special topics are offered in the form of short courses, seminars, and workshops. Students may take these offerings, by permission of the instructor, for variable credit. The course may be taken more than once.
GEOG 706.subject: GEOG
GEOG 706.title: Selected Topics in Cartography and Remote Sensing

GEOG 709.description: Examines in geographical and historical contexts the activities of various women travelers and explorers.
GEOG 709.subject: GEOG
GEOG 709.title: Women Explorers and Travelers

GEOG 710.description: Review of recent literature on geography education with an emphasis on the national geography standards, spatial thinking and the use of geospatial technology in pedagogic contexts.
GEOG 710.subject: GEOG
GEOG 710.title: Seminar in Geography Education

GEOG 711.description: An analysis of the total geographic complex of selected major world regions.
GEOG 711.subject: GEOG
GEOG 711.title: Seminar in Regional Geography

GEOG 712.description: An investigation into the concepts of the urban field and the urban region.
GEOG 712.subject: GEOG
GEOG 712.title: Urban Geography

GEOG 713.description: Investigation into the locational aspects and the spatial systems of selected economic activities, from both regional and systematic viewpoints.
GEOG 713.subject: GEOG
GEOG 713.title: Advanced Economic Geography

GEOG 720.description: The physical and human geography of major world regions with emphasis on basic principles of regional geography. Cannot be used in M.A., M.S., or Ph.D. programs in geography.
GEOG 720.subject: GEOG
GEOG 720.title: World Regional Geography for Teachers

GEOG 721.description: Studies of the characteristics, processes, and distributions over the world of the different cultural and physical environmental elements, such as economic, political, or social activities, climate and landforms.
GEOG 721.subject: GEOG
GEOG 721.title: Seminar in Systematic Geography

GEOG 730.description: Review of recent geographic literature on nature-society interactions with an emphasis on identifying research themes and methodologies employed by contemporary geographers.
GEOG 730.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in GEOG 530, GEOG 568, or equivalents.
GEOG 730.subject: GEOG
GEOG 730.title: Seminar in Environmental Geography

GEOG 731.description: Advanced quantitative approaches for handling and interpreting geographically related data. Multivariate procedures applicable to a variety of problems will be presented. For each topic the students will analyze data relating to their individual interests.
GEOG 731.subject: GEOG
GEOG 731.title: Seminar in Quantitative Analysis in Geography

GEOG 734.description: The student works in a developing country for two to four months on projects designed by instructor and funded by the host country.
GEOG 734.subject: GEOG
GEOG 734.title: Field Seminar in Third World Development Projects

GEOG 735.description: Intensive discussion of classic and contemporary works in the field of political geography.
GEOG 735.subject: GEOG
GEOG 735.title: Seminar in Political Geography

GEOG 740.description: Seminar on research trends and writing research proposals in geography.
GEOG 740.subject: GEOG
GEOG 740.title: Research Trends in Geography

GEOG 741.description: A seminar to familiarize students with current experimental techniques, literature, and research topics in cartography.
GEOG 741.subject: GEOG
GEOG 741.title: Seminar in Cartography

GEOG 746.description: Major theories, measures of climatic change and variability, climate models, statistical analysis, and climate impacts.
GEOG 746.subject: GEOG
GEOG 746.title: Seminar in Climatology

GEOG 747.description: Investigation of physical systems and processes at the earth’s surface. Topics vary; landforms, hydrology, pedology, biogeography, quaternary science, human impacts on physical systems.
GEOG 747.subject: GEOG
GEOG 747.title: Seminar in Physical Geography

GEOG 751.description: Introduction to the fundamental principles and methods of digital image processing of remotely sensed data. Algorithms are discussed for preprocessing, enhancement, and classification mapping of digital data for agricultural, urban, geological, and environmental problems.
GEOG 751.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: GEOG 551 and course in computer programming.
GEOG 751.subject: GEOG
GEOG 751.title: Digital Techniques of Remote Sensing

GEOG 755.description: Satellite-based information extraction; programming skills for digital image processing; self-developed modeling approaches; quantitative analysis of remote sensing data.
GEOG 755.subject: GEOG
GEOG 755.title: Remote Sensing Modeling and Analysis

GEOG 763.description: Theory and application of modern automated approaches to handling geographic data. Includes computer oriented procedures for the input, analysis and display of spatial data.
GEOG 763.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in GEOG 563 or equivalent.
GEOG 763.subject: GEOG
GEOG 763.title: Seminar in Geographic Information Systems

GEOG 801.description: A survey of (1) the philosophical and intellectual foundations of Geography as a discipline, and (2) contemporary ideas and debates in major subfields of geographic research.
GEOG 801.subject: GEOG
GEOG 801.title: Historical and Contemporary Geographic Thought

GEOG 805.description: Advanced directed research by a PhD student on geographical topics to be individually supervised by graduate faculty. This course may be taken for 1-3 credit hours of independent study by a student working closely with a faculty member on a specific research project to be defined and agreed upon between the student and a supervising faculty member.
GEOG 805.subject: GEOG
GEOG 805.title: Advanced Directed Individual Studies in Geography

GEOG 810.description: Reading intensive seminar focused on conceptual frontiers and methodological debates in contemporary human geography with a secondary emphasis on intradisciplinary and cross-disciplinary affinities.
GEOG 810.subject: GEOG
GEOG 810.title: Advanced Seminar in Human Geography

GEOG 811.description: Advanced reading and discussion of the physical, economic, social and/or cultural geography of major selected world regions.
GEOG 811.subject: GEOG
GEOG 811.title: Advanced Seminar in Regional Geography

GEOG 830.description: A research seminar where students critically evaluate relevant literature, develop a research proposal, and complete a related research project in environmental geography.
GEOG 830.subject: GEOG
GEOG 830.title: Advanced Seminar in Environmental Geography

GEOG 841.description: A topic central to cartography will be studied. Students will critically evaluate pertinent literature, develop a research proposal, and complete a related research project.
GEOG 841.subject: GEOG
GEOG 841.title: Advanced Seminar in Cartography

GEOG 847.description: Research and discussion on various topics in physical geography. Literature varies with seminar topic but will include prevailing theories, data types, and modeling strategies in climatology, meteorology, hydrology, biogeography, soils, or geomorphology.
GEOG 847.subject: GEOG
GEOG 847.title: Advanced Seminar in Physical Geography

GEOG 851.description: Advanced reading and discussion in the following areas - 1) the theoretical bases of remote sensing; 2) remote sensing of biophysical variables such as plant and soil temperatures and moisture content; 3) advanced principles of optical and digital image processing; and 4) economic aspects of remote sensing of the environment.
GEOG 851.subject: GEOG
GEOG 851.title: Advanced Seminar in Remote Sensing

GEOG 863.description: A research seminar in which students conduct a detailed analysis of specific aspects of geographical data handling. This will include the design, implementation, and management of an operational geographical information system.
GEOG 863.subject: GEOG
GEOG 863.title: Advanced Seminar in Geographic Information Systems
